# Purchasing Voter Data

## Purchasing Voter Registration Lists

The State Board of Elections maintains voter registration files for 24 local boards of elections and is authorized to sell, to qualified voters, their voter registration lists (mainly statewide registration lists).

To apply for voter registration lists the applicant must:

- [Complete the online application here](https://results.elections.maryland.gov/voter_registration/data_form.html).
- [Download, print and complete the required application (PDF)](https://results.elections.maryland.gov/voter_registration/documents/VR_List_Request_Form.pdf) (this document will print on letter size paper)

Before we will process your application, you must sign a statement, under penalty of perjury, that you will not use the list for commercial solicitation or any other purpose not related to the electoral process. You can use the data to register voters, form a political party, qualify as a candidate for public office, circulate a petition, conduct elections and recount, cast and count ballots, finance a campaign, and other activities that meet the definition of "electoral process" as defined in COMAR 33.03.02.01B(1). You cannot use this data for investigations into illegal or suspected illegal infractions or violations of voters' behaviors in a specific election.

If you would like multiple lists, you must complete an application for each list.

We will provide the data you requested within 10 working days after we receive the application and payment. We can provide the data via FTP, we can mail you the data (on a flash drive), or you can pick up a flash drive with the requested data.

The State Board of Elections and local boards of elections do not guarantee that the data requested will be compatible with all software programs. You must use your own software to import this data to your database. Technical support and special data formats are not provided.

### Deadline to Submit Application:

Applications must be received on or before the advanced voter registration deadline (21 days before an election) or after election day. Applications received after the advanced voter registration deadline will be returned to the applicant.

### Product Information and Cost

- Data can be provided via FTP, mailed on a flash drive, or you can pick up a flash drive with the requested data.
- Cost: $125.00 for each statewide list or $75.00 each for a single county, district, or municipality list.
- If requesting a smaller list, such as a municipality, it may be more affordable to request this data from the Local Board of Elections directly.
- [Payment Site](https://www.velocitypayment.com/client/maryland/sbe/index.html)

# Maryland responds to feds’ request for voter data with step-by-step guide to process

###### By: [Maryland Matters Staff](https://marylandmatters.org/author/maryland-matters-staff/ "Posts by Maryland Matters Staff")-August 5, 2025 12:43 am

[Bluesky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Maryland%20responds%20to%20feds%E2%80%99%20request%20for%20voter%20data%20with%20step-by-step%20guide%20to%20process%20https%3A%2F%2Fmarylandmatters.org%2F2025%2F08%2F05%2Fmaryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process%2F "Bluesky")[X](https://x.com/intent/post?text=Maryland%20responds%20to%20feds%E2%80%99%20request%20for%20voter%20data%20with%20step-by-step%20guide%20to%20process&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarylandmatters.org%2F2025%2F08%2F05%2Fmaryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process%2F&via= "X")[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmarylandmatters.org%2F2025%2F08%2F05%2Fmaryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process%2F "Facebook")[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmarylandmatters.org%2F2025%2F08%2F05%2Fmaryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process%2F&title=Maryland%20responds%20to%20feds%E2%80%99%20request%20for%20voter%20data%20with%20step-by-step%20guide%20to%20process "LinkedIn")[Email](mailto:?subject=Maryland%20responds%20to%20feds%E2%80%99%20request%20for%20voter%20data%20with%20step-by-step%20guide%20to%20process&body=https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/maryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process/ "Email")[Link](https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/maryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process/# "Link")

[![](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/FZM0FtDXkAEBJrN-1536x1139.jpg)](https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/maryland-responds-to-feds-request-for-voter-data-with-step-by-step-guide-to-process/)

Mail ballots received by the Montgomery County Board of Elections during the 2022 primary are sorted during a ballot canvass. (File photo courtesy Montgomery County Board of Elections)

Maryland election officials responded to a Justice Department request for the state’s voter rolls and procedures for maintaining them with a detailed description of election laws and directions on how federal officials could look up the publicly available information for themselves.

The [six-page letter](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Response_Letter_07302025.pdf) from the Maryland State Board of Elections, dated July 30, was in response to a July 14 letter from the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division asking for evidence that the state is “complying with the statewide voter registration list maintenance provisions of the National Voter Registration Act.”

The [letter to Maryland](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/DOJ_Letter_07142025.pdf) was just one of a number of letters that Justice has sent to states probing the integrity of voter rolls. So far, those letters have mostly targeted Democrat-led states, but federal officials told the National Association of Secretaries of State that they expect to eventually reach all 50 states and the District of Columbia with their requests.

Maryland Elections Administrator Jared DeMarinis responded with a detailed description of state and federal laws that dictate how state and county election officials [maintain voter rolls](https://elections.maryland.gov/voter_registration/list_maintenance.html) and remove anyone who is ineligible to vote.

That includes getting “records of deaths, convictions and name changes from state and Federal agencies,” sharing that information with county election officials, contacting any voters on those lists and canceling a voter’s registration “when statutorily-required conditions are met.” The letter went on to note that state law includes safeguards against prematurely removing a voter from the rolls.

> [Justice Department demand for state voter lists underscores their importance](https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/justice-department-demand-for-state-voter-lists-underscores-their-importance/)

Justice Department demand for state voter lists underscores their importance - Maryland Matters

[Justice Department demand for state voter lists underscores their importance](https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/justice-department-demand-for-state-voter-lists-underscores-their-importance/)

[![](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Alabama-voter-600x400.jpg)](https://marylandmatters.org/2025/08/05/justice-department-demand-for-state-voter-lists-underscores-their-importance/)

The Trump administration’s effort to get voter registration lists and other information from states — eventually all of them, officials say — underscores how state-controlled voter lists are a major battleground in fights over access to the polls.

[![](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/logo_footer-148x150.png)Maryland Matters](https://marylandmatters.org/)

“Improper cancellation leads to disenfranchisement of an eligible voter. That is why it is a detailed process. It must be certain,” DeMarinis said in the letter. “Maryland’s process errs on the side of removing any doubt in the cancellation before potentially disenfranchising a voter.”

But the Justice Department letter raised questions about the state’s efforts to purge duplicate and ineligible voters — including those who are dead, convicted or undocumented.

The feds’ letter requested voter registration data from November 2022 to November 2024. It also also asked the state to provide “the number of voters identified as ineligible to vote” during that period as a “non-citizen, … adjudicated incompetent” or because they had a felony conviction. Federal attorneys set a 14-day deadline for state officials to provide the information.

DeMarinis said the state was reviewing mailing records cited in the Justice Department letter, but would not be able to meet the two-week deadline to respond. In response to the Justice Department’s request for the state’s current voter registration list, however, DeMarinis said federal officials could download that data on their own, pointing them to the state page on [purchasing voter data](https://elections.maryland.gov/voter_registration/data.html) and the directions to do so.

The state also downplayed the findings of an October 2023 audit of voter roll maintenance by the Office of Legislative Audits, which cited the possibility of double registrations or possibly [deceased residents](https://www.marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SBE23.pdf) who remained on state voter rolls. State elections officials at the time said [auditors exaggerated](https://marylandmatters.org/2023/11/03/audit-raises-concerns-about-efforts-to-purge-the-dead-from-voter-rolls/) those claims, and DeMarinis last week pointed to his office’s response to the audit then. That response spelled out the state’s rigorous process of cross-checking registrations that, in the case of duplicate registrations, found “at most a potential 0.00645% rate of duplicates among all active Maryland voter registration records.”

The Justice Department letter was one of two the state received last month, demanding information on voter registration and on state and county election officials efforts to keep the rolls up to date and free of unqualified voters. The [second letter](https://marylandmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Maryland-NVRA-Letter.pdf), received four days after the Justice Department request, came from lawyers representing a group of local, state and national Republicans who alleged “implausibly high” levels of voter registration, both statewide and in some individual counties.

The GOP letter, directed to the state board and boards of election in Howard and Montgomery counties, threatened to “bring a lawsuit” against the state and local boards “if you fail to take specific actions to correct these violations” within 90 days.

State and local officials said last month that they were still reviewing that letter. But DeMarinis last week, in his letter to the Justice Department, expressed confidence that the system of keeping accurate voter rolls, while protecting the “sacred right” to vote, is sound.

“The State Board works diligently to ensure that every eligible Marylander can register to vote in accordance with federal and state laws,” he wrote. “And as referenced above, election officials in Maryland continue that diligent work to maintain up to date voter rolls.”

**Mail-In Ballot Replacement Information** \- Up to date information from the [State Board of Elections](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/2026_replacement_mib.html)

Further information from [Montgomery County Board of Elections (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/Voter%20services/Replacement-Ballots-Mailed-to-Affected-Montgomery-County-Voters-5-28-2026.pdf).

# State and County Board of Elections' Services

## County Board of Election Services

### PRODUCTS

The Montgomery County Board of Elections (address: 18753 North Frederick Avenue Suite 210, Gaithersburg, MD 20879) provides a variety of products for public information. Many items are free of charge and are readily available; others must be ordered in advance and prepaid. There is a $25 charge for returned checks.

[VOTER REGISTRATION INFORMATION](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseOne)

All voter registration data is reported as of the first of the month. **_Voter registration information provided by the Board of Elections may not be used for purposes of commercial solicitations_ or for any other purpose not related to the electoral process (Election Law Article, § 3-506, Annotated Code of Maryland).**

**[APPLICATION TO VIEW THE VOTER REGISTRY (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/registration/APPLICATION%20TO%20VIEW%20THE%20VOTER%20REGISTRY%20March_16_2026.pdf)**

The completed request may be mailed to Montgomery County Board of Elections, emailed to **[Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov)** or faxed to 240-777-8600.

[**APPLICATION FOR COUNTY-WIDE VOTER REGISTRATION (PDF)**](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/registration/APPLICATION%20FOR%20COUNTY-WIDE%20VOTER%20REGISTRATION%20INFORMATION%20REV%20March_16_%202025.pdf)

**Instructions for ordering county-wide voter registration information:**

[**VOTER REGISTRATION FILE INSTRUCTIONS (PDF)**](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/registration/VoterRegistrationFileReadMe.pdf)

**Note: To view and print PDF documents, you must have Adobe Acrobat Reader. You can download the [Adobe Acrobat Reader](https://get.adobe.com/reader/) for free.**

[MAIL-IN BALLOT LABEL DATA FILE](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseTwo)

[**MAIL-IN BALLOT LABEL DATA FILE (PDF)**](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/Products_Services/MIB_Label_Application_2026.pdf)

Electronic list for mail-in ballot voters is available once the mail-in ballots have arrived at the Board of Elections. The list of mail-in ballot voters is provided twice weekly until the last Thursday before Election Day.  An application must be completed and a request must be submitted in advance. A request for mail-in ballot voter list continues for an entire election cycle and may  not be canceled. Please call the Board of Elections for information concerning the distribution schedule of mail-in ballot label files.

The Vote By Mail label file is in EXCEL format, and includes the following data:

- Countywide
- Congressional District
- Legislative District
- Council District
- Board of Education District
- Party affiliation

Delivery: All electronic list transmission.

For more information, contact Nora L. Dorsey, Program Specialist II – Voter Registration at **[laletta.dorsey@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Laletta.Dorsey@montgomerycountymd.gov)**

[CERTIFICATION OF VOTER REGISTRATION](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseThree)

Certification of Registration is official verification of voter registration in Montgomery County, embossed with the Montgomery County Seal.

Cost: $1 per certificate, payment by cash or check (make checks payable to: Montgomery County, Maryland); prepayment is necessary if mailed.

For more information, please call 240 777 8500 or email **[Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov)**

[DUPLICATE VOTER NOTIFICATION CARD](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseFour)

The Voter Notification Card is a confirmation of a current voter's information (name, address, party affiliation, district or precinct boundary, polling place, and accessibility).

Cost: $1 per duplicate voter notification card, payment by cash or check (make checks payable to: Montgomery County, Maryland); prepayment is necessary if mailed.

For more information, please call 240-777-8500 or email **[Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Voter.Registration@montgomerycountymd.gov)**

[ELECTION MAPS](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseFive)

Street maps of various district boundaries are available. In addition to streets and district boundaries, the maps show roads, hydrology and other visible entities. Payment is made by cash or check. Prepayment is necessary if mailed maps are requested.

Map sizes: Small - 8 1/2" x 11".  Large - 34" x 44"

Map prices:

Single small Precinct Map = $ .25

Large County or District Maps = $20

Free: Small countywide maps

Mailing costs depend on volume, tubes and USPS rates.

Maps are available for the following districts:

- Congressional
- Legislative
- Councilmanic
- Board of Education
- Precinct

For more information, contact Louise Warner, GIS Mapping Specialist at **[louise.warner@montgomerycountymd.go](mailto:louise.warner@montgomerycountymd.gov) v**

* * *

### SERVICES

The Board of Elections provides a variety of services to aid citizens in exercising their right to vote; to provide information to candidates and potential candidates for public office about filing for office and campaign funding; and to furnish information to the general public about candidates, elections, and accessibility to polling places.

[PERMANENT MAIL-IN BALLOT LIST](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapseSix)

A list of voters who requested permanent mail-in ballots (for future elections) is available upon request.  The list, if provided in an electronic format via email, is free of charge. The list is also available in electronic format on a USB flash drive for a charge of $10, payable by cash or check. If the list cannot be emailed (due to the file size or other restrictions) it will only be provided on a USB flash drive for the above set charge

An [**Application**](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/registration/Permanent%20Mail%20In%20Ballot%20List%20Application%2003_16_2026.pdf)  to request the list of permanent mail-in ballot voters must be completed, signed, and returned:

- via email to Ms. Michelle Gonda at  [michelle.gonda@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:barbara.payne@montgomerycountymd.gov) or
- mailed to  Montgomery County Board of Elections 18753 N. Frederick Avenue, Suite 210  Gaithersburg, Maryland 20879

Once the initial request is processed, the updated list will be provided per the schedule below:

- At the beginning of each month in a non-election year.
- At the beginning and middle of each month in an election year until six weeks prior to Election day;
- Once a week starting six weeks before Election Day.

_Note: If the scheduled date falls on a weekend or a holiday, the list is prepared on the next business day._

The permanent mail-in ballot file is in EXCEL format, and includes:

- Voter ID
- Last Name, First Name, Middle Name, Suffix
- Status
- Residential Address
- Precinct
- Mailing Address
- Political Party

To create a subset of the data by congressional, legislative, council or Board of Education district, use the Precincts Within District lists found **[here](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/PrecinctDescriptionsCharts/PrecinctDescriptionCharts.html)**.

For more information, contact Ms. Michelle Gonda at  [michelle.gonda@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:barbara.payne@montgomerycountymd.gov)

[RECEIVED MAIL-IN BALLOT LIST](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#received-mail-in-ballot)

A list of voters whose mail-in ballots were received by the Montgomery County Board of Elections is available upon request. The list, if provided in an electronic format via email, is free of charge. The list is also available in electronic format on a USB flash drive for a charge of $10, payable by cash or check. If the list cannot be emailed (due to the file size or other restrictions) it will only be provided on a USB flash drive for the above-set charge.

An [Application (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/registration/Received%20Mail%20In%20Ballots%20List%2003_16_2026.pdf) to request the list of voters whose mail-in ballots were received by BOE must be completed, signed, and returned:

- via email to Ms. Michelle Gonda at [michelle.gonda@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:barbara.payne@montgomerycountymd.gov) or
- mailed to Montgomery County Board of Elections 18753 N. Frederick Avenue, Suite 210  Gaithersburg, Maryland 20879

Once the initial request is processed, the updated list will be provided per the schedule below:

- On the first Friday after the legal deadline to mail ballots to voters on the permanent mail-in ballot list and voters who requested mail-in ballots at least sixty (60) days before the election.
- Every subsequent Friday until the Election Day.

The permanent mail-in ballot file is in EXCEL format, and includes:

- Voter ID
- Last Name, First Name, Middle Name, Suffix
- Received Date
- Mail-in ballot Status
- Mail-In Ballot Address
- Precinct
- Political Party

To create a subset of the data by congressional, legislative, council or Board of Education district, use the Precincts Within District lists found [here](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/PrecinctDescriptionsCharts/PrecinctDescriptionCharts.html).

For more information, contact Ms. Michelle Gonda at [michelle.gonda@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:barbara.payne@montgomerycountymd.gov)

[OFFICIAL SAMPLE BALLOT & VOTERS GUIDE](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapse8)

The Official Sample Ballot & Voters Guide is mailed to all registered voters in Montgomery County approximately one week before early voting begins for each Primary and General Election. The sample ballot is the ballot style the voter is required to vote for ​each election. The ​Primary election ballot style is based on the voter's residential address ​and party affiliation on record. ​The General election ballot is based on the voter's residential address only.  Large-type sample ballots are available upon request. An online sample ballot is available as part of the [Voter Lookup service of the State Board of Elections](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch) .

- [Congressional District 4 - Official Sample Ballot and Voting Information, 2024 Presidential General Election (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/Sample%20Ballots%20and%20Voter%20Guide/2024-presidential-general/sample-ballot-congressional-4.pdf)
- [Congressional District 6 - Official Sample Ballot and Voting Information, 2024 Presidential General Election (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/Sample%20Ballots%20and%20Voter%20Guide/2024-presidential-general/sample-ballot-congressional-6.pdf)
- [Congressional District 8 - Official Sample Ballot and Voting Information, 2024 Presidential General Election (PDF)](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Resources/Files/pdfs/Sample%20Ballots%20and%20Voter%20Guide/2024-presidential-general/sample-ballot-congressional-8.pdf)

For more information, contact Gilberto Zelaya, Community Empowerment/Public Information Officer at [gilberto.zelaya@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Gilberto.zelaya@montgomerycountymd.gov)

[POLLING PLACE](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapse9)

The Board of Elections designates a polling place for every precinct. Where possible, the polling place is in the precinct and accessible. A registered voter is assigned a polling place based on residence information provided by the voter.

- Accessibility for Registered Voters with Disabilities - If you are a voter with a disability, you may request reassignment to an accessible polling place. The request must be in writing and made no later than the close of voter registration (three weeks before the election day). The reassigned polling place has the same ballot style as that of the initially assigned polling place.
- Polling Place Lists - Two lists, polling place names in alphabetical sequence and polling place precinct numbers in numerical sequence, are available on this website, [http://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/voting-locations.html](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/voting-locations.html), or hard copy may be purchased for $1.50 each at the Board of Elections office.

For more information, contact Ms. Mindy Williams, Polling Place Manager via email: [mindy.williams@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:mindy.williams@montgomerycountymd.gov)

[CANDIDATE INFORMATION](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/Information/Products.html#collapse10)

The Board of Elections provides candidate services and information including qualifications for office, candidacy filing requirements, deadlines, forms, and campaign finance regulations and reports.

For information pertaining to candidate information, please visit the [State of Maryland Board of Elections - Candidacy web page](https://elections.maryland.gov/candidacy/index.html).

"Requirements for Filing as a Candidate \- a packet containing the following information will be provided to interested individuals:

- A listing of all elected offices for Montgomery County and the State of Maryland; qualifications for the offices and filing fees
- Filing requirements for all offices; a list of required documents and where to obtain them; how, when, and where to file
- Fund-raising account options; types of accounts; when fundraising may begin; necessary forms; qualifications, duties and responsibilities for Campaign Chairman and Campaign Treasurers
- A summary of requirements regarding campaign activity

Candidate List:

The Maryland State Board of Elections maintains a current list of all candidates who have filed in Montgomery County for the next election; the list may also include candidates filed with the State Board of Elections in Annapolis. For more information [click here](http://www.elections.state.md.us/elections/2018/index.html)

Copies of Campaign Fund Reports for Montgomery County Candidates:

Copies of Campaign Fund Reports for Montgomery County candidates are available for inspection by the public. Photocopies cost $ .25 per page if copied by elections office staff.

Payment: Cash or check

[Elected Officials List](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/Elections/Information/electedofficials.html)

A list of elected officials and their addresses, telephone numbers, FAX numbers, and e-mail addresses is available free of charge on web [www.777vote.org.](https://mcg.montgomerycountymd.gov/elections/index2.html)

Election Calendar:

Election calendars from the State Board of Elections are available free of charge at the Board of Elections.

Financial Disclosure Information:

For information pertaining to Maryland State financial disclosure [click here](http://ethics.gov.state.md.us/)

Political Signs:

The Board of Elections provides brochures from the Montgomery County Department of Permitting Services and the [State Highway Administration](https://www.roads.maryland.gov/pages/faqs.aspx?CatId=0&QId=26) which explain the requirements of the Montgomery County zoning ordinances regulating the size, placement, and removal of political campaign signs, as well as regulations on posting signs adjacent to State highways.

For more information, contact Michelle Gonda via email at [Michelle.Gonda@montgomerycountymd.gov](mailto:Michelle.Gondat@montgomerycountymd.gov)

# Voter Lookup

We update this website daily. If you submitted information today, you will not be able to see it yet. If you submitted information online or at the MVA, it may take up to 3 weeks to appear on this website.


You can use this tool to:

- Review your voter registration record.
- Request a duplicate voter registration card.
- Find out where to vote.
- Find out your voting districts.
- Find out your local board of elections.
- See the status of your mail-in or provisional ballot.
- View your sample ballot.

Search
Based on what you entered, we were unable to find any information.

Before trying again, please:

- Enter your name the same way you registered to vote. For example, if you registered to vote as “Jeff” instead of “Jeffrey,” use “Jeff” for the search.
- If you moved recently, enter the zip code where you lived before.
- If you changed your name recently, enter your former name.
- If you believe you are registered but you still cannot find your information, [contact your local board of elections.](http://www.elections.maryland.gov/about/county_boards.html)
- If you have not registered before, you may [register to vote online.](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/OnlineVoterRegistration)

Remember that it may take up to 3 weeks after your registration was submitted for the data to get posted to this site.

First Name:

Provide your first name as it appears on your voter registration record.


First name is required and may contain only letters and spaces.

Last Name:

Provide your last name as it appears on your voter registration record.


Last name is required and may contain only letters, hyphens, and spaces.

Date Of Birth:

Provide your date of birth as it appears on your voter registration record.


Month:Day:Year:

Please enter a valid month, it should be a number between 1 and 12.Please enter a valid date, it should be a number between 1 and 31.Please enter a valid year, it should be a number between 1921 and 2010Date of Birth is required. Make sure you have entered the date correctly.

Zip Code:

Provide the 5 digit zip code of the Maryland residential address provided on your voter registration record.

Zip code is required and must be exactly 5 numeric characters.

Street Number:

Provide the street number of the Maryland residential address provided on your voter registration record. Letters and 1/2 indicators are not necessary.

Street number must contain only numbers, letters, commas, hyphens, and forward slashes.

Middle Initial:

Provide your middle initial as it appears on your voter registration record.

Middle initial can be only a single alpha character.

# Board of Elections

## Specimen Ballot Press Release

Prince George’s County Board of Elections announced today that the local distribution of physical specimen ballots for the 2026 Primary Election is successfully underway across the county. Following minor logistical adjustments at the printing level, the U.S. Postal Service began processing and shipping the ballots out in continuous waves starting on Wednesday, June 10, 2026.

[Read the full press release from the Prince George's County Board of Elections](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/Specimen%20Ballot%20Press%20Release.pdf "Specimen Ballot Press Release")

## Mail-In Ballot Replacement Information

Due to an error in the printing process, some voters received the incorrect party ballot for the Gubernatorial Primary Election. This error affects only voters who were mailed a ballot before May 14, 2026. All affected voters will be mailed a replacement ballot.

[Read the full update from the Maryland State Board of Elections](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/2026_replacement_mib.html)

## Mission

The Prince George's County Board of Elections seeks to promote voter education, administer an efficient voting process, maintain an accurate voter registration database, and ensure that elected officials are elected in accordance with Federal, State, and County election laws.

## Responsibilities

The Board of Elections is responsible for supervising elections, voter registration, and record keeping, and the administration of election laws in Prince George's County in accordance with the [Election Law Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland](https://elections.maryland.gov/laws_and_regs/election_law.html). The Board and the Election Administrator seek to provide voter registration to every County citizen who wants it.

## 2026 Gubernatorial Election

[Filed Candidates](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/CF%20006%202026%20GUB%20PRIMARY%205.19.26.pdf "CF 006 GUB Primary 5.19.26")

[Sample Ballots](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/PG%20Sample%20Ballots%20GUB%202026.pdf "Sample Ballot GUB 2026")

[MD-VoterGuide-Primary 2026 English](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/MD-VoterGuide-Primary%202026%20-%20English.pdf "MD VotersGuide-Primary 2026 English")

[MD-VoterGuide-Primary 2026 Spanish](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/MD-VoterGuide-Primary%202026%20-%20Spanish.pdf "MD VoterGuide-Primary 2026 Spanish")

### (((Primary Election Results)))

**Early Voting**\- June 11, 2026 through June 18, 2026 (7am - 8pm)

**Election Day** \- June 23, 2026 - 7am - 8pm

[Primary Election Results](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/Primary_results/gen_results_2026_by_county_17.html)

### General Election

**Early Voting** \- October 22, 2026 through October 29, 2026 (7am - 8pm)

**Election Day** \- November 3, 2026 - 7am - 8pm

[2026 Drop Box Locations](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/DROP%20BOX%20LOCATONS%202026%20Gubernatorial.pdf "Drop Box Locations 2026 Gubernatorial")

### Your Voter Information

Use the [Maryland State Board of Elections Voter Lookup](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch) tool to find your current voter registration and district information.

[Check Your Voter Registration](https://voterservices.elections.maryland.gov/VoterSearch)

## Current County Districts, Precincts, and Polling Places

[**2026 Polling Place Changes**](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/2026%20Polling%20Place%20Changes.pdf "2026 Polling Place Changes")

[**District - Precincts - 2026**](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/2026%20-%20District-Precincts%20-%20327%20-%20Updated_0.pdf "2026-District-Precincts-327")

[**2026 Early Voting Sites**](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/sites/default/files/media-document/2026%20Early%20Voting%20Sites%20-13%20sites.pdf "2026 Early Voting Sites - 13 sites")

The Prince George's County Board of Elections wants to ensure that all eligible voters in our county can access the polls fairly and equally. To support this effort, we keep a contact list of people and organizations who want to know when Local Board Meetings will discuss changes to polling place locations.

**If you want to receive notifications about attending these meetings, please complete the Polling Place Change Notification Form.**

[Polling Place Change Notification Form](https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/89bc59f8f57e4bc7a878014dfc015281)

## Board of Elections Meetings

The next [board meeting](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/departments-offices/events/hearingmeeting/2026/06/june-8th-2026-prince-georges-county-board-elections-board-meeting-virtual "June 8th, 2026, Prince George's County Board of Elections' Board Meeting - Virtual") will be conducted (virtual) on Monday, June 8th, 2026, at 5:30 pm.

Prince George's County Board of Elections

1100 Mercantile Lane, Suite 115A

Largo, MD 20774

### Agendas & Minutes

Agendas are available before the meetings. Minutes are available after approval.

[View All Agendas and Minutes](https://www.princegeorgescountymd.gov/government/county-government/agendas-minutes?year=&field_event_start_value_1=&field_event_end_value=&field_boards_commissions_target_id_1=466#center-3090678413)

### Board Meeting Videos

[Link to join board meeting livestream via Microsoft Teams](https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/19%3ameeting_NTI5YmU3MGItOTAwZS00ZDdkLTkxMGUtOTEzZjcwMDFmNDg1%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b%22Tid%22%3a%224146bdda-ddc1-4d2a-a1b2-1a64cc3c837b%22%2c%22Oid%22%3a%229fcc06a3-c30e-4fc0-b5f9-3d44fc23e0c4%22%7d)

Beginning in June 2025, board meetings will be livestreamed, and videos of the board meetings will be made available for review on our YouTube channel. Videos of board meetings will be posted and published as soon as possible.

[View All Board Meeting Videos](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLi6YomQwclK0k9cHQSIQm6nBsqePDrPaq)

## Board Members

The Governor, by and with the consent of the Senate, appoints five people who constitute the Board of Elections. The appointees are selected from lists provided by the County Central Committee of the Democratic and Republican parties. The Board is responsible for the supervision of all County, State, and Federal Elections held in Prince George's County.
